full_name: Institut national pour l'évaluation et la sécurité de l'intelligence artificielle
mission: INESIA federates four national bodies — ANSSI (cybersecurity agency), Inria (digital-science research institute), LNE (national metrology and testing lab) and PEReN (digital-regulation expertise unit) — to build public expertise in evaluating and securing advanced AI. It develops evaluation methods, supports implementation of the EU AI Act, studies systemic risks and represents France in the international network of AI safety institutes.

key_work.title: Feuille de route INESIA 2026–2027 (roadmap)
key_work.plain_summary: Sets INESIA's priorities: sovereign evaluation capacity for advanced AI, support for the AI Act, systemic-risk analysis, knowledge sharing and international cooperation.

key_work.title: Évaluer et sécuriser l'IA (SGDSN mission page)
key_work.plain_summary: Explains why evaluation of complex AI systems has become strategic, including for national security.

key_work.title: Government announcement creating INESIA
key_work.plain_summary: Press release (31 Jan 2025) launching the institute in line with the 2024 Seoul Declaration.

status_note: announced 31 Jan 2025 ahead of the Paris AI Action Summit; jointly steered by SGDSN (Prime Minister's defence and security secretariat) and the DGE (economy ministry). Adopted its 2026–2027 roadmap on 12 Feb 2026. It is a network of existing bodies, not a standalone agency.
status_raw: active — announced 31 Jan 2025 ahead of the Paris AI Action Summit; jointly steered by SGDSN (Prime Minister's defence and security secretariat) and the DGE (economy ministry). Adopted its 2026–2027 roadmap on 12 Feb 2026. It is a network of existing bodies, not a standalone agency.
funding_note: Uses existing budgets of its member bodies under SGDSN/DGE steering.

warnings.text: The most advanced AI systems are reaching unprecedented complexity, making risks hard to assess.
AI raises national-security issues, including cybersecurity of AI systems and systemic risks.

recommendations.text: Build a rigorous, independent public capacity to evaluate advanced AI that works with European and international efforts.
Support AI Act implementation with scientific evaluation methods.
Cooperate with other institutes (e.g. a 2026 Franco-German agreement with Germany's new AI safety and security institute).
